unfold.unfolded: Let $S$ be an ordered semigroup and $m\ge 1$ an integer. A subsemigroup $B$ of $S$ is an $m$-bi-ideal of $S$ if $BS^mB\subseteq B$ and $(B]=B$, where $(X]=\{x\in S : x\le y \text{ for some } y\in X\}$ and $S^m$ is the set of all products of $m$ elements of $S$. The integer $m$ is called the bipotency of the bi-ideal $B$.
notes: The closure (X] is not defined in the context; the usual definition is used.
The naming of m as the bipotency of B is restored, as the original states it.

verdict.reason: The unfolded form states the same conditions for a subsemigroup to be an m-bi-ideal and spells out the standard meanings of (B] and S^m. It also preserves the statement that m is its bipotency.
